content: Hydroxyzine, when combined with other substances, can lead to various pharmacodynamic interactions. Below are the detailed interactions and their clinical implications: 1. Hydroxyzine and ethanol: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Hydroxyzine and etomidate: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 3. Hydroxyzine and ezogabine: Both increase the QTc interval. Monitor the QTc interval, especially when ezogabine is titrated to higher doses (e.g., 1200 mg/day). Co-administration with other QT-prolonging agents requires ECG monitoring. 4. Hydroxyzine and fenfluramine: Hydroxyzine increases sedation, while fenfluramine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 5. Hydroxyzine and fentanyl: Either drug can increase the toxicity of the other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with anticholinergics may increase the risk of urinary retention, severe constipation, or paralytic ileus. 6. Hydroxyzine and fingolimod: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 7. Hydroxyzine and flibanserin: Both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely, as the risk of sedation is heightened when flibanserin is combined with other CNS depressants. 8. Hydroxyzine and fluconazole: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 9. Hydroxyzine and fluphenazine: Both increase sedation and the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 10. Hydroxyzine and flurazepam: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 11. Hydroxyzine and fluvoxamine: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 12. Hydroxyzine and formoterol: Hydroxyzine increases sedation, while formoterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 13. Hydroxyzine and fostemsavir: Both increase the QTc interval. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. Use caution and monitor. 14. Hydroxyzine and gabapentin: Either drug can enhance the effects of the other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration of CNS depressants can result in serious, life-threatening respiratory depression. Use the lowest effective dose and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 15. Hydroxyzine and ganaxolone: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 16. Hydroxyzine and gemifloxacin: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 17. Hydroxyzine and gemtuzumab: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 18. Hydroxyzine and gilteritinib: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 19. Hydroxyzine and givinostat: Both increase the QTc interval. Obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 20. Hydroxyzine and glycopyrronium tosylate (topical): Either drug can enhance the effects of the other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration with other anticholinergic medications may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. 21. Hydroxyzine and goserelin: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 22. Hydroxyzine and gotu kola: Gotu kola enhances the effects of hydroxyzine through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor, as it may enhance CNS depression. 23. Hydroxyzine and granisetron: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 24. Hydroxyzine and haloperidol: Both increase sedation and the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 25. Hydroxyzine and hawthorn: Hawthorn enhances the effects of hydroxyzine through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor, as it may enhance CNS depression. 26. Hydroxyzine and histrelin: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 27. Hydroxyzine and hops: Hops enhance the effects of hydroxyzine through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor, as it may enhance CNS depression. 28. Hydroxyzine and hyaluronidase: Hydroxyzine decreases the effects of hyaluronidase. Large systemic doses of antihistamines may render tissues partially resistant to hyaluronidase, requiring larger amounts for equivalent dispersing effects. Use caution and monitor. 29. Hydroxyzine and hydromorphone: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 30. Hydroxyzine and hyoscyamine: Both decrease cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor. 31. Hydroxyzine and iloperidone: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 32. Hydroxyzine and imipramine: Both increase sedation and the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 33. Hydroxyzine and incobotulinumtoxinA: Hydroxyzine enhances the effects of incobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor, as drugs with anticholinergic effects may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 34. Hydroxyzine and inotuzumab: Both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Obtain a baseline ECG to assess the initial QT interval and determine the frequency of subsequent monitoring. Avoid non-essential QT-prolonging drugs and correct electrolyte imbalances. 35. Hydroxyzine and isoproterenol: Hydroxyzine increases sedation, while isoproterenol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. 36. Hydroxyzine and itraconazole: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 37. Hydroxyzine and ketamine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 38. Hydroxyzine and ketotifen (ophthalmic): Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 39. Hydroxyzine and lapatinib: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 40. Hydroxyzine and lasmiditan: Either drug can enhance the effects of the other through sedation. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been evaluated in clinical studies. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse reactions. 41. Hydroxyzine and lemborexant: Either drug can enhance the effects of the other through sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Dosage adjustment may be necessary if lemborexant is co-administered with other CNS depressants due to potentially additive effects. 42. Hydroxyzine and letibotulinumtoxinA: Hydroxyzine enhances the effects of letibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor, as drugs with anticholinergic effects may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 43. Hydroxyzine and leuprolide: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 44. Hydroxyzine and levetiracetam: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 45. Hydroxyzine and levocetirizine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 46. Hydroxyzine and levofloxacin: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 47. Hydroxyzine and levomethadyl: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 48. Hydroxyzine and lithium: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 49. Hydroxyzine and lofepramine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 50. Hydroxyzine and loperamide: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. This list provides a detailed overview of hydroxyzine's interactions with various drugs and substances.
